summary: Paul says if I speak with tongues of men and angels but don't have love, I am noisy gong, nothing, if I have all faith to move mountains but not love nothing, if give all goods and body to be burned but not love nothing. Love is patient kind, not envious boastful arrogant rude self-seeking irritable, not keep record of wrongs, not rejoice in unrighteousness but in truth, bears believes hopes endures all, love never fails. Tongues will cease, knowledge will be done away, we know in part, prophesy in part, when perfect comes imperfect done away, now see in mirror dimly then face to face, now faith hope love abide but greatest love.
whyItMatters: Most famous chapter on love, read at weddings, but written to correct church that prized spectacular gifts over character — love as greatest, never fails, way to use gifts. Defines love not as feeling but as patient action.

themes: love is patient kind not envious boastful

questions.question: Why does Paul say without love I am nothing even if I speak tongues of angels, have all faith, give everything?
questions.answer: Corinth prized impressive gifts — tongues, prophecy, knowledge, faith to move mountains, radical generosity and martyrdom (give body to be burned). Paul says without love they are noisy gong (pounds without melody) and zero. Love is not addition to gifts but condition that gives gifts value. For community that competed over gifts, it's correction: character over charisma.

questions.question: What does love definition — patient, kind, not envious, not boastful — mean in practice?
questions.answer: Greek gives 15 verbs: positive — patient (makrothumei long-tempered), kind (chresteuetai useful), rejoices in truth; negative — not envious (zeloi, jealous), not boastful (perpereuetai, brag), not arrogant (phusioutai puffed), not rude, not self-seeking, not irritable, not recording wrongs (logizomai — accounting term). It's habit, not feeling — how love acts when irritated, envious, wronged. For zero-background: read as job description for love, not emotion.

questions.question: What does 'bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things' mean? Isn't that naive?
questions.answer: Four alls: stego — covers, protects like roof; pisteuei — trusts, gives benefit of doubt; elpizei — hopes, doesn't give up; hypomenei — endures under load. Not gullible (believes everything anyone says) but within community, love gives benefit of doubt, hopes best, endures. Not naive optimism but resilient commitment that doesn't keep ledger of wrongs (v5).

questions.question: What does 'when perfect comes imperfect done away, now see in mirror dimly then face to face' mean?
questions.answer: Mirror in ancient world was polished bronze, dim reflection, not clear glass. Now we know in part, prophesy in part — like seeing dimly. When perfect (teleion) comes — mature, complete, often read as when Christ returns or when love complete — partial ceases. Then face to face — not dim reflection but direct encounter, fully known as fully known. Childhood vs adulthood analogy: now think like child, then adult. Love remains after gifts cease.

questions.question: Why 'faith hope love remain, greatest is love'?
questions.answer: After gifts cease, three remain. Faith, hope, love are theological virtues. Love greatest because faith becomes sight and hope becomes possession when face to face, but love continues — God is love, so love is eternal. Also, love is what makes faith and hope work — without love, faith is nothing (v2). For Corinth debating gifts, love is greatest because it builds community, never fails (v8), while gifts temporary.

glossary.def: Greek for love as action, commitment, not just eros feeling — patient, kind, enduring.
Pounding bronze, like gong without melody — impressive noise without love.
Polished bronze mirror giving dim reflection — now partial, then face to face clarity.
